title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: ngram-mod self-speculation on top of MTP, and repeat-penalty 1.0
setup: Temporary router, same conditions as qwen36-mtp-draft-length.json. 'edit-tool' is a realistic agent load: one call to an `edit` tool whose old_string is copied from the context and whose new_string contains the change. Three code fragments, 1 seed. All variants keep `spec-draft-n-max 2`.

variants.label: MTP 2 + ngram-mod 12/12/32 (server warns: n_match too small)

replication_table.description: Replication with 3 fragments x 3 seeds (9 requests per variant and load); only edit-tool and edit.

repeat_penalty_alone.description: Quick batch (copy, edit, reasoning), 1 seed: repeat-penalty 1.1 (starting point) vs 1.0.

no_effect: CPU threads (2/4/8/16) and busy-poll: within +-3% noise
batch/ubatch other than 2048/1024: ubatch 2048 is 23-28% slower at prompt processing
KV cache type f16 vs q8_0: same speed (q8_0 uses half the memory)
ngram-map-k: 57.7 vs 59.3 tok/s mean (quick batch of copy, edit, reasoning): no gain over MTP alone
probabilistic draft sampling and draft-p-min: +2-8% on copy/edit, losses on reasoning
source: Internal report 29 (2026-10-23), sections 'ngram, repeat-penalty' and 'tuning of the n-gram and the edit tool call'.
